clue.text: It's preferable without, for example, a father

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for preferable surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: preferable means better

explanation.surface: Someone muses that it would be better to manage without a father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; the surface reading of doing without a father is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To beget is to father a child, so one who begets is a father in the archaic biblical sense.

clue.text: Two lads find someone to bully

parts.note: Vic is a boy's name, the first of the two lads
Tim is a boy's name, the second of the two lads

explanation.surface: Two boys go looking for somebody they can pick on.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim is the target of a bully, the person someone picks on.

clue.text: Duke takes poor girl to initiate nunnery and church

parts.note: a Poor Clare is a nun of the order founded by St Clare, so the poor girl is Clare

indicators.note: the initial, or opening letter, of the word nunnery is what is taken

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A duke escorts an impoverished young woman to found a convent and a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor girl' points to the Poor Clares, an order of nuns, so the girl is CLARE; 'to initiate' takes the first letter of nunnery.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarence is a British royal dukedom, held for instance by the Duke of Clarence drowned in malmsey.

clue.text: Perform heartless ditty as a soloist

parts.note: to perform a song is to sing

indicators.note: the central letter of the short song word is removed, as if its heart were cut out

parts.note: a lay is a short song or ballad

explanation.surface: A singer is told to deliver a soulless little song alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle letter A from LAY, a poetic word for a song, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Singly means one by one or alone, which is how a soloist performs.

clue.text: One Soviet cop beyond the Pyrenees

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police, the NKVD

explanation.surface: A Russian secret policeman is spotted over the mountains in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen from France, the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal lies on the far side of the Pyrenees.

clue.text: What infirm setter has to live on?

definitions.text: What infirm setter has to live on?

parts.note: read as two words, in firm, giving IN plus CO, the abbreviation for company
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A frail crossword compiler wonders what money he will survive on.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'infirm' into 'in firm' for IN + CO; the setter is ME. The whole clue then describes earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is the money a person lives on, from wages, pension or investments.

clue.text: Fish completely frozen

parts.note: all can mean completely, as in all alone
frozen water is ice

explanation.surface: Some seafood is reported to be frozen solid.
explanation.definitionFit: The allice, or allis shad, is a herring-like European fish that swims up rivers to spawn.

clue.text: Old writ makes English run

parts.note: leg it is slang for run away

explanation.surface: An old legal document prompts an Englishman to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegit was a historical writ letting a creditor take a debtor's land until the debt was paid.

clue.text: Vocal tribute to Japanese camper van?

definitions.text: Vocal tribute to Japanese camper van?

parts.words: Vocal tribute to Japanese camper van?
parts.note: a famous tenor aria is imagined as a song in praise of a Nissan Dormobile, a Japanese-made camper van, the title sounding like those brand names

explanation.surface: Someone sings the praises of a motorhome made in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: The Puccini aria from Turandot sounds like Nissan (Japanese carmaker) plus dormer, the start of Dormobile, a British make of camper van.
explanation.definitionFit: The aria from Turandot is a sung piece, here jokingly cast as homage to a vehicle.

clue.text: Once called to exercise on a bike, first to fall off

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it
the opening letter of the riding word drops away, as a cyclist might tumble off

parts.note: to cycle is to ride a bike
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to get fit by cycling, and the leader takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to fall off' drops the opening C of the riding word, leaving YCLE. Yclept is a deliberately archaic word, signalled by 'Once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yclept is an archaic past participle meaning named, so it fits once called.

clue.text: About to get work over in good time for tea

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for in good time goes round the rest

parts.note: early means in good time

indicators.note: over signals that the unit of work is turned back to front

parts.note: the erg is a scientific unit of work

explanation.surface: Someone is about to start a job and finish punctually for afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the unit of work back to front, giving GRE. 'About' looks like 'roughly' but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a black tea blend flavoured with bergamot.

clue.text: Throw out by a fraction of a semitone

indicators.note: only a part of the musical word is taken, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A singer misses the note by a small musical interval.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or send out, as with light or sound.

clue.text: Pregnant woman needs a little drill?

definitions.text: Pregnant woman needs a little drill?

parts.words: Pregnant woman needs a little drill?
parts.note: an expectant mother wants some exercises, but the real sense is a drill attachment for boring into brick

explanation.surface: An expectant mother is advised to do some light exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill' looks like antenatal exercise; it is the power tool, and the tip used on brick or stone. The question mark flags wordplay in 'Ma's on', a mother expecting.
explanation.definitionFit: A masonry bit is a tungsten-tipped drill attachment for boring brick and stone.

clue.text: It's OK for one who's jilted

definitions.text: It's OK for one who's jilted

parts.words: It's OK for one who's jilted
parts.note: the two letters in the centre of the word for smashed are O and K, and the phrase also describes the grief of someone dumped by a lover

explanation.surface: Someone reassures a person who has just been dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of BROKEN is OK, so the clue's 'OK' is literally a 'broken heart'; that is also what the jilted lover suffers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being jilted leaves a person with deep emotional pain, the classic heartache of rejection.

clue.text: Mayor entertains boy in Lincs.

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take him in, so one name goes inside the other

parts.note: Ken Livingstone was the first Mayor of London
Steve is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A civic leader hosts a lad somewhere in Lincolnshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone was London's mayor when this appeared; Kesteven is a district of Lincolnshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Kesteven is one of the historic parts of Lincolnshire, so it lies within that county.

clue.text: Criminal on the phone

definitions.meaning: a ... of stolen goods, a fence, is a criminal
the handset part of a telephone, held to the ear

explanation.surface: A crook is caught talking on the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Receiver means both a handler of stolen goods and the handset piece of a telephone.

clue.text: No drinks plugs for wood spirits

parts.note: a dry event serves no alcohol
plugs are advertisements, ads

explanation.surface: With alcohol banned, the woodland ghosts are advertised instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryads are tree nymphs of Greek myth, spirits living in woods.

clue.text: Gothic writer who fuels the flames

definitions.meaning: Bram ... wrote the Gothic novel Dracula
one who shovels coal into a furnace

explanation.surface: A horror novelist also keeps the fire going.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoker names both the Dracula author and a person tending a furnace or boiler.

clue.text: Sudden inspiration this month or in 17

indicators.note: in means the other pieces are placed inside the writer's forename

parts.note: 17 down's writer was Bram Stoker, so his first name is used
inst. is the old commercial abbreviation for instant, meaning this month
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bright idea strikes this month, or perhaps while reading a horror writer.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAM is Bram Stoker's forename from 17; 'inst' is business shorthand for this month. INST and OR go inside BRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainstorm is a sudden burst of ideas or a flash of inspiration.

clue.text: Grass performing well?

definitions.meaning: to grass is slang for ... on someone to the police
a sportsman playing well is said to be ...

explanation.surface: A snitch is doing rather well.
explanation.definitionFit: Inform means to grass on someone, and read as two words describes good form.

clue.text: Pain causes sullen note at first

indicators.note: at first puts the musical note ahead of the other piece

parts.note: me, or mi, is the third note of the sol-fa scale
grim means sullen or forbidding

explanation.surface: A gloomy musical note brings on suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: Me is the sol-fa note also spelt mi. The grid printed MEGRIN, but the dictionary word is MEGRIM, an old name for a migraine.
explanation.definitionFit: A megrim is an old word for a migraine, a severe headache.

clue.text: Name making sound sense

indicators.note: the word for a sense is said out loud and the spelling changes

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Someone makes their meaning clear by naming the point.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to name or quote something as an example or authority.

clue.text: Harm felt badly — pupils are not now 19

indicators.note: something done badly is botched or garbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A school break, when children are no longer in class, does some damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is INFORM, read as 'in form': at this school holiday pupils are not in their form classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Half term is the short school holiday mid-term in Britain, when pupils are away from their classes.

clue.text: Composer walking about topless

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the remaining letters are shuffled
the first letter of walking is removed, as if its top came off

explanation.surface: A composer strolls around without a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes W from walking, leaving ALKING; 'about' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Glinka was a Russian composer, regarded as the father of Russian classical music.

clue.text: World put about confection virtually 6

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
an orb is a sphere, a globe or world

explanation.surface: Someone places a globe around a sweet treat that is nearly frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is ALLICE; a sorbet is virtually an ice, the second part of that answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a frozen dessert of fruit and sugar, very nearly an ice cream.

clue.text: Play keeping in one-dimensional form

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the play surrounds the small word

parts.note: King Lear is a Shakespeare play
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre production holds on to a flat, one-dimensional style.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear describes something along a single line, having just one dimension.
